newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Borotra wants world currency pact.
newsitem.headline: France's Borotra wants world currency pact.

text.p: French industry minister Franck Borotra said on Monday he wanted the world's powers to agree on a global currency pact, otherwise, a general competitive equilibrium would be lost.

"Internationalisation has become the rule. I am very attached to freedom of exchange as long as the rules of reciprocity and fairness between partners are respected," he said during a meeting of a regional chamber of commerce.
"The reproach that I make to the European Union is that they are too often very naive, and they do not use fully the commercial defence weapons against competitors who behave in an unfair way.
"It is necessary that the big trading partners put on the table monetary practices because without that, the general exchange equilibrium is being endangered."
Borotra said the single European currency was the sole lever to show to the United States the continent was serious about taking up the competitive challenge.
He also said Europe should not be so naive as to open up the European market to countries engaging in unfair competition like competitive devaluations of their currencies.
